causal-factors.name: Active election-petition mechanism in Sabah (Sindumin case and Sabah petitions)
causal-factors.rationale: Election petitions have been filed against Sabah poll results (Sindumin petition filed December 2025; subsequent petitions reported), showing a viable path to overturn results in Sabah if irregularities are proven. (Malay Mail, 2025-12-27; The Borneo Post, 2025-12-31)

causal-factors.name: Lamag margin of victory in the January 24, 2026 by-election
causal-factors.rationale: Mohd Ismail Ayob won Lamag by 5,681 votes (7,269 to 1,588), a large margin that historically lowers overturn risk, though not guarantees immunity. (Malay Mail, 2026-01-24; Sinar Harian, 2026-01-24)

causal-factors.name: Historical overturn precedents (Malaysia) show overturns are possible
causal-factors.rationale: Past cases like Kuala Terengganu 2023 show an election can be declared void if corruption or illegal practices are proven. (Wikipedia, 2023-06-27; Malay Mail, 2023-09-26)

causal-factors.name: Petitions can be dismissed; not all petitions overturn results
causal-factors.rationale: A number of petitions in Malaysia have been dismissed or not pursued to overturn results (e.g., Bukit Gelugor 2014; Tasek Gelugor 2018), indicating a non-negligible chance that a Lamag petition could fail. (The Borneo Post, 2014-09-23; Malay Mail, 2018-09-18)

causal-factors.name: Lamag victory margin
causal-factors.rationale: The Lamag by-election was won by BN with a large majority (7,269 to 1,588), a 5,681-vote margin, which lowers the probability of overturn.

causal-factors.name: Active Sabah election petitions (Sindumin and others)
causal-factors.rationale: Election petitions have been filed in Sabah seats like Sindumin, indicating a live mechanism that could challenge results, including by-elections.

causal-factors.name: Historical overturn precedents in Malaysia
causal-factors.rationale: There are precedents where results were overturned (e.g., Kuala Terengganu 2023), which keeps overturn risk nonzero.

synthesis: The base ensemble assigns a small chance of overturn (3%), but Sabah’s petition ecosystem and historical precedents introduce a nonzero risk. The large Lamag margin and absence of an overturn by May 2026 make such an outcome unlikely, though not impossible; the calibrated probability sits modestly above the ensemble.
